issues.description: Method parameter mismatch for Rideable.messageOnRide: the problem statement UML and template usage expect a no-argument method messageOnRide() returning String, and the template Main calls r.messageOnRide() with no arguments. The solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) (and Pig/Seal implement messageOnRide(int)), which requires an int parameter. This inconsistency will cause compilation errors or force students to choose between implementing the no-arg signature required by the spec/template or the int-parameter signature present in the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable API consistent across all artifacts. Preferred: change the solution to define Rideable.messageOnRide() with no parameters and update Pig and Seal implementations to implement public String messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]" (matching the UML and template usage). Alternatively, if an int speed parameter is intended, update the problem statement, UML, template Main (calls) and all instructions to require messageOnRide(int speed) and show the expected output format including speed.

issues.description: The Rideable interface's messageOnRide method is named and typed differently across artifacts. In the problem statement and the provided template Main, the interface/method is described and used as messageOnRide() with no parameters (problem_statement.md defines Rideable.messageOnRide():String and Main.java calls r.messageOnRide()). In the solution repository, Rideable is declared as messageOnRide(int speed) and the implementing classes Pig and Seal implement messageOnRide(int speed). Students following the problem text and template will implement and call a no-argument method, but the solution uses a method with an int parameter, causing a direct signature mismatch and blocking a clear mapping between requirement and implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the Rideable API across artifacts. Preferred fix (maintains the problem statement and template behavior): change the solution repository to declare `String messageOnRide()` in Rideable (no parameters) and update Pig and Seal to implement this no-argument method, returning the string format described in the problem (e.g., "Riding on Pig [name]" and "Riding on Seal [name]"). Alternatively, if the intended design requires a speed parameter, update the problem statement and template to document and call `messageOnRide(int speed)` and update examples accordingly. The recommended action is the first option to match the problem statement and template usage.
